project.purpose: External-first Game LEGO research and substitution without legacy games.

nodes.label: ExternalKnowledge
nodes.behavioralContract: Provenance-bound; no automatic new Game law.
acceptance: Source class and provenance retained.

nodes.label: MechanismExperiences
nodes.behavioralContract: Advisory candidates cannot reject novel compositions.
acceptance: Falsifier, source and transfer scope recoverable.

nodes.label: RelationshipProjection
nodes.behavioralContract: Rebuildable view; never a closed game ontology.
acceptance: Graph rebuild and retrieval equivalence.

nodes.label: CounterexampleMemory
nodes.behavioralContract: No automatic blacklist or design recommendation authority.
acceptance: Sources and failure context retained.

nodes.label: KnowledgeQueries
nodes.responsibility: Use existing source-bound retrieval interfaces without a Game service
nodes.behavioralContract: No current game is selected; retrieval never establishes player enjoyment or runtime permission.
acceptance: Query tests and knowledge closure pass.

nodes.label: NativeAssemblyAcceptance
nodes.responsibility: Check a concrete Godot composition of state, actions, event observation and native resource/scene substitution
nodes.authority: Game source owner and upstream Godot runtime
outputs: test evidence for bounded transitions and component substitution
nodes.behavioralContract: Only the configured finite scene, resource contract and tested native signal/scene seams are validated. No universal game, player-value or third-party script safety proof.
acceptance: Pinned Godot headless example boots as a real PackedScene.
Bounded action exhaustions preserve state invariants and goal behavior.
Player Resource and alternate presentation PackedScene substitute without changing rules; invalid configuration is rejected atomically.

nodes.label: BevyNativeProductAssembly
nodes.responsibility: Compose one game-specific engine-independent Rust rule machine with upstream Bevy ECS, Plugin, input, sprite and text systems
nodes.authority: Game product rules owner; Bevy upstream engine owns ECS, renderer, schedules and input
outputs: bounded Rust rule and Bevy system test evidence
nodes.behavioralContract: Goal collection, hazard damage and restart are game-owned transitions; Bevy-native systems consume those rules. Cargo compile and test do not prove rendered GPU output or human enjoyment.
acceptance: Pin the actual Bevy version and Cargo.lock.
Native Rust rule and Bevy Plugin/system tests pass.
Compile Bevy application with cargo check --locked --all-targets; physical player input/output remains unverified without a graphical run.

I: Bevy app schedule and keyboard events
O: Bevy ECS changes, Sprite/Text projections and compiled application
S: RunState phase, collected goals, lives and last-hit time
pre: Bevy =0.20.1 and Cargo.lock source dependencies available
target and initial lives are positive
post: collect-all leads to Won; exhausted lives lead to Lost; restart makes a fresh run in the bounded tested rule domain
inv: terminal rules do not mutate collected/lives
engine-native ECS and rendering retain upstream ownership
eff: Bevy ECS world state, native window and graphics effects when launched; current source verifies compile/tests but not an installed graphical session
recursiveLegoR21.c: Rule transitions O(1); ECS/frame scheduling and renderer cost depend on runtime/scene and are not measured
recursiveLegoR21.epsilon: Graphical runtime, frame rate, input latency and human experience are UNKNOWN; compile PASS is not graphical execution proof

nodes.label: GodotMovementAudioFeedback
nodes.responsibility: Subscribe to real native Godot gameplay turn transitions and play source-licensed replaceable WAV feedback without owning gameplay state
nodes.authority: Game effect adapter owns event-to-play mapping; Godot owns AudioStreamPlayer and lifecycle; Kenney owns licensed source assets
inputs: AudioStreamWAV loaded from a source-qualified asset
outputs: AudioStreamPlayer playback request on accepted turn advance
nodes.behavioralContract: Only a turn strictly advancing from the last observed turn requests audio; resets and rejected actions do not trigger audio; substituting AudioStream leaves rules unchanged.
acceptance: main.tscn owns the audio node and ordinary scene startup binds its actual rule signal.
Real key input advances state and initiates playback; rejected input has no rule or audio effect.
Another actual WAV replaces the resource without changing GridRules; headless verification produces no leaked audio resources.
mustNotOwn: claims about audible physical output or player enjoyment

pre: a live Godot AudioStreamPlayer, loaded stream and bound GridRules signal
post: strict increase of turn causes one playback call; no increase causes none
inv: GridRules alone owns legal-action admission and game state
AudioStream replacement leaves rule transitions unchanged
recursiveLegoR21.c: Constant work per state-change notification; actual audio-device scheduling cost not measured
recursiveLegoR21.epsilon: Physical speaker rendering, perceptual latency, accessibility and player-value effects UNKNOWN
prov: examples/native-composition/assets/kenney-ui-audio/README.md with pinned original CC0 source and two WAV SHA-256 hashes

slices.objective: Preserve external-first mechanism/reference knowledge without a game product.
acceptance: Source-bound knowledge remains retrievable.
No prior executable game survives.

slices.objective: Existing query tools consume the registered knowledge.
acceptance: Read-only queries execute and do not create new products or proof claims.

slices.objective: Native Game state/action/observation composition is runnable and independently substitutable at Godot Resource and PackedScene seams.
acceptance: Native Godot headless acceptance passes and the project main scene boots.
No old game product or new general-purpose mod framework is added.

slices.objective: Use real source-locked Bevy Plugin/ECS for one bounded game-specific Rust ruleset, not a generic engine
acceptance: Cargo rule tests and Bevy compilation pass.
Physical renderer/window and human play remain explicitly UNKNOWN.

slices.objective: Compose source-licensed native audio feedback into the ordinary Godot game scene through its real state-change signal
acceptance: The ordinary main.tscn boots with actual audio resource and rule binding.
Real right-key transition, invalid action and substitute WAV pass native Godot execution; no claim of physical audio quality.
